newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end weaker on Dow, interest rate fears.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end weaker on Dow, interest rate fears.

text.p: Malaysian shares closed weaker on Friday after a 140-point fall on Wall Street and fears of higher Malaysian interest rates in 1997, analysts said.
The benchmark Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks closed 5.67 points lower to 1,217.64.
"The fall in the U.S. coincided with the 30-year bond yield to reach 7.1 percent, which means that rates here may have to go up," said William Chan, a dealer at Seagroatt and Campbell.
Analysts speculated that the Malaysian government would hint at a tightening of monetary policy in the central bank's annual report due to be published at 0900 GMT on Friday.
The release of trade data earlier in the day, showing a deficit of 95.5 million ringgit in January 1997 against a 1.1 billion deficit in January 1996, had little impact on prices, dealers said.

"The market reacted to possible restrictions on bank loans to the property market, share financing (announced in the Bank Negara 1996 annual report) and the weaker Wall Street," said Victor Wan, senior analyst at South Johor Securities.
Timber stocks were active, with Tekala and Aokam among the most actively traded stocks. Tekala gained 90 cents to 8.40 ringgit, while Aokam lost 10 to 5.85.
